scenario: [LNUL.3.4] — a `Json?` slot holds the canonical null the ordinary way. Two asserts of Python None into a nullable Json payload both land; their `id` keys differ, so they are two entities (LFAC.1.7.2) and both facts stay live. Named for the LFAC.1.3 heading (`ttl` facts), which it does not test; its schema is `logical`. Dedup on null has no expressible schema: a root-null Json document is the canonical null ([LNUL.3.4]), so a `Json` slot refuses it as it refuses any null, and [LNUL.8.10] forbids a nullable identity key. A root-null Json document is not expressible from this harness (Python None is the canonical null itself), so that half is pinned in C, by runtime/tests/libds/spec/test_null_spec.c::test_lnul_3_4__root_null_json_is_the_canonical_null and runtime/tests/libds/impl/test_lnul_3_4_root_null_json.c, and in the Mercury runtime's test_ds: a root-null document is the canonical null, refused in `Json` and stored as null in `Json?`, and `{"a": null}` is still a legal document.
